<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" id="h-we-uncover-the-truth-and-hold-the-powerful-to-account">We uncover the truth and hold the powerful to account. </h2>



<p class="has-text-align-center">Do you believe we have a shared humanity and a shared responsibility for what goes on in the world, despite what politicians tell us?</p>



<p class="has-text-align-center"><strong>If you do, then you’re one of us.</strong></p>

</div></section>

<section id="section-29a8847c" class="section" style=""><div id="29a8847c" class="container">

<div class="wp-block-columns is-layout-flex wp-container-core-columns-is-layout-9d6595d7 wp-block-columns-is-layout-flex">
<div class="wp-block-column is-vertically-aligned-center is-layout-flow wp-block-column-is-layout-flow">
<p>Our unwavering belief in the power of people united has brought about <strong>real change</strong>, stretching across every corner of the world. Thanks to years of support from committed supporters like you, the death penalty is abolished in most countries, dangerous spyware used to target activists has been uncovered and seemingly untouchable tyrants have been made to answer for their crimes.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-who-is-amnesty-international">Who is Amnesty International?</h3>



<p>Amnesty International is a <strong>global movement of more than 10 million people </strong>who are committed to creating a future where human rights are enjoyed by everyone. United by our <strong>shared humanity</strong>, we know that the power to create positive change is within all of us. </p>



<p>We are funded by members and <strong>people like you</strong>. We are independent of any political ideology, economic interest or religion. We stand with victims of human rights violations <strong>whoever they are, wherever they are.</strong></p>



<p>No government is beyond scrutiny. <strong>We uncover the truth.</strong> We hold human rights violators to account.</p>
</div>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-our-mission-and-statute">Our mission and statute</h2>
<p>We have a vision of a world where everyone can <strong>enjoy the human rights enshrined in the <a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/what-we-do/universal-declaration-of-human-rights/">Universal Declaration of Human Rights</a> </strong>and other international human rights mechanisms. To achieve this vision, our mission is to undertake <strong>research and action focused on preventing and ending grave abuses</strong> of these rights. </p>
<p>Our core values are rooted in our commitment to the global community of human rights defenders that make up our membership:</p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>International solidarity</li>
<li>Effective action for the individual victim</li>
<li>Global coverage</li>
<li>Universality and indivisibility of human rights</li>
<li>Impartiality and independence </li>
<li>Democracy and human rights</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="wp-block-column is-vertically-aligned-center is-layout-flow wp-block-column-is-layout-flow">
<div style="height:25px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>

<div id="d380546f" class="container">
<div class="wp-block-columns is-layout-flex wp-container-core-columns-is-layout-9d6595d7 wp-block-columns-is-layout-flex">
<div class="wp-block-column is-vertically-aligned-top is-layout-flow wp-block-column-is-layout-flow">
<div style="height:25px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>
<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-our-strategic-plan">Our strategic plan</h2>
<p>Our offices across the globe are guided by a shared strategic plan that establishes key priorities and values that empower us to work together more effectively.</p>
<p>The current Global Strategic Framework covers our work from 2022 to 2030. It designates key human rights priorities, common lenses that we apply across all work and core capabilities that we rely on to remain effective.</p>
<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow">
<summary>Our human rights priorities</summary>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-priority-1-freedom-of-expression-and-civic-space">Priority 1 – Freedom of expression and civic space</h3>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>1.1 – Strengthening freedom of expression and association</li>
<li>1.2 – Securing the right to peaceful assembly for all</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-priority-2-equality-and-non-discrimination">Priority 2 – Equality and non-discrimination</h3>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>2.1 – Promoting gender, racial and intersectional justice</li>
<li>2.2 – Strengthening enjoyment of rights to health, housing and social security</li>
<li>2.3 – Securing climate justice</li>
<li>2.4 – Protecting the rights of refugees and migrants and the rights of people on the frontlines of crises</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-flexible-areas-of-work">Flexible areas of work</h3>
<p>In addition to work on Global Priorities 1 and 2, Amnesty International entities may dedicate up to 20% of its resource to work on <strong>Flexible Areas of Work </strong>– human rights issues chosen in response to other pressing local human rights concerns, for example ending the death penalty, access to justice and redress, and preventing human rights abuse within the criminal justice system. </p>
</details>
<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow">
<summary>Common lenses</summary>
<p>In all the work that we do, whether under the Global Priorities or flexible areas of work, Amnesty will analyse, plan and evaluate our human rights work through the following common lenses: </p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>Individuals and communities at risk </strong>– Working with and for individuals and communities at direct risk of human rights violations.</li>
<li><strong>Intersectionality, gender-mainstreaming and anti-racism</strong> – Focus strongly on people subjected to structural discrimination on multiple and intersecting grounds, including, among others, the grounds of gender identity, race, ethnicity, class and other forms of social origin, caste, First Nations/Indigenous identity and sexual orientation.  Analyse the human rights implications of discrimination and clearly incorporate the findings into documentation, recommendations and campaign demands. </li>
<li><strong>Corporate accountability, including for the technology sectors </strong>– Analyse the roles of corporate actors and, on that basis, work to ensure states legislate mandatory human rights due diligence requirements for corporations, hold them accountable for their part in human rights abuses, and provide remedy to their victims.</li>
</ul>
</details>
<details class="wp-block-details is-layout-flow wp-block-details-is-layout-flow">
<summary>Strengthening Amnesty’s capabilities</summary>
<p>Within the period of the Strategic Framework 2022-2030, in support of its human rights priorities, Amnesty will strengthen and evolve our ability to deliver human rights change, as follows:</p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-stakeholders-perspective">Stakeholders perspective</h3>
<p><em>What do we need to do with our stakeholders to achieve our outcomes?</em></p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Acting in solidarity with individuals and communities facing human rights challenges and supporting their demands</li>
<li>Influencing and enabling duty bearers to uphold their obligations legally and in practice</li>
<li>Influencing and enabling corporates to limit the negative impacts on human rights and explore different ways of engaging</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-capabilities-perspective">Capabilities perspective</h3>
<p><em>How will we innovate and invest to engage our stakeholders?</em></p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Mobilizing human rights education</li>
<li>Enhancing human rights research</li>
<li>Delivering compelling state and corporate advocacy</li>
<li>Strengthening Amnesty people powered movement and visibility</li>
<li>Enhancing our work with partners</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-internal-processes-and-learning-perspective">Internal Processes and Learning Perspective</h3>
<p><em>What will help us engage our stakeholders?</em></p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Grounding our work on international human rights law and Amnesty policies</li>
<li>Strengthening our movement by improving our infrastructure and processes</li>
<li>Investing in the well-being of our members and staff and in equality and inclusion</li>
<li>Increasing and improving our understanding of impact and evidence-based decision making</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-financial-perspective">Financial Perspective</h3>
<p><em>How can we sustain and increase our resources?</em></p>
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Growing our resources and income to be financially sustainable based on our values.</li>
</ul>
<p>You can find more information about how Amnesty finances work in our Strategic Framework on our <a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/about-us/how-were-run/finances-and-pay/">finances page</a>.</p>
</details>
</div>

<div class="wp-block-columns is-layout-flex wp-container-core-columns-is-layout-9d6595d7 wp-block-columns-is-layout-flex">

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-how-are-we-governed">How are we governed?</h2>
<p><strong>Amnesty International runs on people power. </strong></p>
<p>We are a democratic organization which means that we are governed by individual members like you. Every year, representatives from <strong>over 60 countries </strong>attend a Global Assembly to vote on decisions that guide the Amnesty movement. These decisions include the <strong>selection of the International Board</strong>.</p>
<p>As an Amnesty member, you can <strong>participate in local conferences, events and elections</strong> organized by your country office. </p>
<p>If you live in a country that does not have an Amnesty office, you can <a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/about-us/international-membership/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">join as an <strong>international member.</strong></a></p>
<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-how-are-we-financed">How are we financed?</h2>
<p>Our deeply held core principles of<strong> impartiality, independence and accuracy underpin all we do. </strong>This is built on an understanding that all human rights must be respected together if we are to achieve a world free from fear and want.</p>
<p>We are <strong>independent of any institution, ideology, economic interest, and religion.</strong> Our only interest is in achieving human rights for all. </p>

https://www.amnesty.org/en/about-us/.visible_text: About Us - Amnesty International About Us - Amnesty International Which language would you like to use this site in? English Español Français العربية 简中 繁中 Русский Close English Español Français العربية 简中 繁中 Русский Who We Are How We’re Run Work with us What We Do Countries Get Involved Take Action Become a member Take an online course Latest News Campaigns Education Research Impact Search Donate Now ul" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="mobile-menu" aria-label="Open navigation" > Who We Are Who We Are How We’re Run Work with us What We Do Countries Get Involved Get Involved Take Action Become a member Take an online course Latest Latest News Campaigns Education Research Impact Search Who We Are © Itzel Plascencia López / Amnistía Internacional México We uncover the truth and hold the powerful to account. Do you believe we have a shared humanity and a shared responsibility for what goes on in the world, despite what politicians tell us? If you do, then you’re one of us. Our unwavering belief in the power of people united has brought about real change , stretching across every corner of the world. Thanks to years of support from committed supporters like you, the death penalty is abolished in most countries, dangerous spyware used to target activists has been uncovered and seemingly untouchable tyrants have been made to answer for their crimes. Who is Amnesty International? Amnesty International is a global movement of more than 10 million people who are committed to creating a future where human rights are enjoyed by everyone. United by our shared humanity , we know that the power to create positive change is within all of us. We are funded by members and people like you . We are independent of any political ideology, economic interest or religion. We stand with victims of human rights violations whoever they are, wherever they are. No government is beyond scrutiny. We uncover the truth. We hold human rights violators to account. Be part of a global movement for human rights Become a member today join us Our mission Our strategy How we’re run Our mission and statute We have a vision of a world where everyone can enjoy the human rights enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and other international human rights mechanisms. To achieve this vision, our mission is to undertake research and action focused on preventing and ending grave abuses of these rights. Our core values are rooted in our commitment to the global community of human rights defenders that make up our membership: International solidarity Effective action for the individual victim Global coverage Universality and indivisibility of human rights Impartiality and independence Democracy and human rights For more information on our statute and mission Read the full statute Read the full statute Our strategic plan Our offices across the globe are guided by a shared strategic plan that establishes key priorities and values that empower us to work together more effectively. The current Global Strategic Framework covers our work from 2022 to 2030. It designates key human rights priorities, common lenses that we apply across all work and core capabilities that we rely on to remain effective. Our human rights priorities Priority 1 – Freedom of expression and civic space 1.1 – Strengthening freedom of expression and association 1.2 – Securing the right to peaceful assembly for all Priority 2 – Equality and non-discrimination 2.1 – Promoting gender, racial and intersectional justice 2.2 – Strengthening enjoyment of rights to health, housing and social security 2.3 – Securing climate justice 2.4 – Protecting the rights of refugees and migrants and the rights of people on the frontlines of crises Flexible areas of work In addition to work on Global Priorities 1 and 2, Amnesty International entities may dedicate up to 20% of its resource to work on Flexible Areas of Work – human rights issues chosen in response to other pressing local human rights concerns, for example ending the death penalty, access to justice and redress, and preventing human rights abuse within the criminal justice system. Common lenses In all the work that we do, whether under the Global Priorities or flexible areas of work, Amnesty will analyse, plan and evaluate our human rights work through the following common lenses: Individuals and communities at risk – Working with and for individuals and communities at direct risk of human rights violations. Intersectionality, gender-mainstreaming and anti-racism – Focus strongly on people subjected to structural discrimination on multiple and intersecting grounds, including, among others, the grounds of gender identity, race, ethnicity, class and other forms of social origin, caste, First Nations/Indigenous identity and sexual orientation. Analyse the human rights implications of discrimination and clearly incorporate the findings into documentation, recommendations and campaign demands. Corporate accountability, including for the technology sectors – Analyse the roles of corporate actors and, on that basis, work to ensure states legislate mandatory human rights due diligence requirements for corporations, hold them accountable for their part in human rights abuses, and provide remedy to their victims. Strengthening Amnesty’s capabilities Within the period of the Strategic Framework 2022-2030, in support of its human rights priorities, Amnesty will strengthen and evolve our ability to deliver human rights change, as follows: Stakeholders perspective What do we need to do with our stakeholders to achieve our outcomes? Acting in solidarity with individuals and communities facing human rights challenges and supporting their demands Influencing and enabling duty bearers to uphold their obligations legally and in practice Influencing and enabling corporates to limit the negative impacts on human rights and explore different ways of engaging Capabilities perspective How will we innovate and invest to engage our stakeholders? Mobilizing human rights education Enhancing human rights research Delivering compelling state and corporate advocacy Strengthening Amnesty people powered movement and visibility Enhancing our work with partners Internal Processes and Learning Perspective What will help us engage our stakeholders? Grounding our work on international human rights law and Amnesty policies Strengthening our movement by improving our infrastructure and processes Investing in the well-being of our members and staff and in equality and inclusion Increasing and improving our understanding of impact and evidence-based decision making Financial Perspective How can we sustain and increase our resources? Growing our resources and income to be financially sustainable based on our values. You can find more information about how Amnesty finances work in our Strategic Framework on our finances page . Global priorities 80% Freedom of expression and civic space and Equality and nondiscrimination Flexible areas 20% Other relevant and emerging human rights issues Read the full 2022-2030 Strategic Framework English Spanish French How are we governed? Amnesty International runs on people power. We are a democratic organization which means that we are governed by individual members like you. Every year, representatives from over 60 countries attend a Global Assembly to vote on decisions that guide the Amnesty movement. These decisions include the selection of the International Board . As an Amnesty member, you can participate in local conferences, events and elections organized by your country office. If you live in a country that does not have an Amnesty office, you can join as an international member. How are we financed? Our deeply held core principles of impartiality, independence and accuracy underpin all we do. This is built on an understanding that all human rights must be respected together if we are to achieve a world free from fear and want. We are independent of any institution, ideology, economic interest, and religion. Our only interest is in achieving human rights for all. Find more information on how Amnesty is funded Our finances Learn more about Amnesty’s leadership Meet our leadership Amnesty International Charity is a company registered in England & Wales, limited by guarantee (no. 02007475) and a registered charity (no. 294230), with registered office at 1 Easton Street, London WC1X 0DW. The charity is a subsidiary of Amnesty International Limited. تحركوا الآن نناضل من أجل عالم يتمتع فيه الجميع بحقوق الإنسان منظمة العفو الدولية حركة عالمية تضم أكثر من 10 ملايين شخص، في ما يزيد عن 150 بلداً وإقليماً، يناضلون من أجل وضع حد لانتهاكات حقوق الإنسان. آخر الأخبار الأخبار إسرائيل/الأرض الفلسطينية المحتلة: إسرائيل تكثّف إجراءات الضم من خلال أوامر غير المشروعة بالاستيلاء على الأراضي في الضفة الغربية المحتلة الأخبار إسرائيل/الأرض الفلسطينية المحتلة: يجب أن يدفع الملف الذي قدّمته جنوب إفريقيا إلى محكمة العدل الدولية الدولَ إلى الضغط على إسرائيل لإنهاء الإبادة الجماعية التي ترتكبها في غزة الأخبار تونس: السبيل القضائي الأخير لإلغاء الإدانات في قضية “التآمر” الظالمة الأخبار الكويت: إجراءات مكافحة الإرهاب المتخذة في ظل الحرب مع إيران تهدد الحقوق الأساسية وتوسّع نطاق عقوبة الإعدام الأخبار فلسطين: على حماس أن تضع حدًا لعمليات الإعدام خارج نطاق القضاء وأن تضمن العدالة للضحايا من نحن منذ 1961 ونحن نساعد الناس على المطالبة بحقوقهم عبر العالم. طالعوا قصتنا ماذا نفعل نحن نوفر الحماية للحقوق الإنسانية للناس، من عقوبة الإعدام إلى حرية التعبير استعرضوا المواضيع شاركوا اكتبوا رسالة، تطوعوا، تبرعوا … وارفعوا صوتكم ضد الظلم حول العالم. بادروا بالتحرك المواضيع الأكثر تداولًا الاحتلال الإسرائيلي للأرض الفلسطينية العدالة الدولية الاختفاء القسري معلومات عنا الاتصال بنا كيف تُدار المنظمة بيان قانون مكافحة العبودية الحديثة الشؤون المالية الموارد المركز الإعلامي التربية على حقوق الإنسان دورات حقوق الإنسان شاركوا معنا انضموا إلينا بادروا بالتحرك تطوعوا معنا آخر المستجدات الأخبار الحملات الأبحاث اعمل معنا إذا كنتم موهوبين ومتحمسين لحقوق الإنسان، فمنظمة العفو الدولية تريد أن تسمع منكم. الوظائف والتدريب سياسة الخصوصية شروط استخدام الموقع الإلكتروني سياسة الكوكيز أذونات استرداد التبرعات © 2026 منظمة العفو الدولية اتبعونا على: X Facebook Instagram TikTok Bluesky LinkedIn YouTube

<p>The International Secretariat is responsible for leading the majority of the organization’s research and campaigning efforts. It also manages supporters and members in countries where no national Amnesty International entities exist.</p>



<p>In countries with national Amnesty International offices, these entities are responsible for managing their own supporters and members. When necessary, we will forward your message or request to the appropriate local Amnesty International organization to ensure you receive the best possible assistance.</p>



<p><em>Please note that due to a lack of resources, we are unfortunately not able to answer queries from academics, students and school children asking for help with their studies. However, all of our reports and publications are available from our <a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/search/">online library</a> and you can find more resources in our <a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/human-rights-education/">section on human rights education.</a></em></p>

It also manages supporters and members in countries where no national Amnesty International entities exist. In countries with national Amnesty International offices, these entities are responsible for managing their own supporters and members. When necessary, we will forward your message or request to the appropriate local Amnesty International organization to ensure you receive the best possible assistance. Please note that due to a lack of resources, we are unfortunately not able to answer queries from academics, students and school children asking for help with their studies. However, all of our reports and publications are available from our online library and you can find more resources in our section on human rights education.
